messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx rate detected for customer OrchidNova on dedicated pool 'us-west3-pool-7' — 5m error rate 18% (baseline 0.3%). Paging on-call.
oncall-sev: on it, grabbing metrics and logs. assigning to oliver.
oliver-sre: seeing p50/p95 token latency rising, KV eviction rate spiking on nodes 7-9. looks like GPU saturation + KV thrash.
mari-dev: any recent deploys for OrchidNova?
jia-eng: none in last 24h. OrchidNova has a large batch inference job running cyclically, maybe started a few hours ago.
oliver-sre: confirmed a heavy batch job from their account started ~2h ago, with sustained long sequences. It pinned multiple GPUs and increased prefix cache churn.
oncall-sev: what's customer impact?
liz-acc: customer reports intermittent 504s and degraded per-request throughput; they opened a ticket at 09:12 PT. High severity for them.
oliver-sre: reproducing error pattern in logs: gateway 504s followed by backend 5xx with message 'kv-cache-miss: eviction-failure' and 'cuda-out-of-memory' on some workers.
mari-dev: can we throttle their burst or move their sessions to a separate pool?
oliver-sre: we have two immediate mitigations: 1) apply a soft concurrency cap on OrchidNova's routes (rate-limit/queue) 2) temporarily reroute new OrchidNova sessions to fallback pool us-west3-pool-2 (lower perf but isolated).
jia-eng: patch route config with quick canary: set max_concurrency=8 for OrchidNova and route-new=true — deploy in 30s?
oncall-sev: go ahead. prefer to avoid redeploying runtime; is route config a live change?
oliver-sre: yes, we can update route metadata via control plane API. doing it now: 
```bash
# update route through control plane
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://control.redwood/api/v1/routes/orchidnova/config \
  -d '{"max_concurrency":8,"route_new_sessions_to":"us-west3-pool-2"}'
```
oliver-sre: applied, propagation starting. watching metrics.
incident-bot: Route config change accepted; propagation to edge in ~12s.
mari-dev: metrics: eviction rate down ~40% on nodes 7-9; p95 latency dropping from 760ms -> 430ms. 5xx rate falling to 6% (still elevated).
jia-eng: reroute seems to take load off pool-7, but pool-2 is now at 65% GPU util. still headroom.
oliver-sre: good. next step: reduce batch size recommendation for their large job (if they can). can we reach out to their job runner?
liz-acc: messaging customer now: "We've applied a temporary concurrency cap and routed new sessions to an isolated pool to reduce errors. Would you be able to reduce the batch size for long-running jobs?"
incident-bot: customer_ticket: #ON-4482 created and linked.
oncall-sev: any memory leaks or infra bug? or purely noisy neighbor?\oljunk: (not present)
oliver-sre: digging deeper — kernel selection shows fallback to less-optimized GEMM in some steps due to memory pressure; seems resource exhaustion not a code bug. noisy neighbor + long sequences.
mari-dev: can we evict long-lived cache entries for OrchidNova prefix keys to reclaim KV?
jia-eng: we can run targeted KV eviction for OrchidNova's namespace during low usage windows, but doing so may increase latency briefly while warming. prefer current routing + concurrency cap until job finishes.
oliver-sre: agree. monitoring for 30m. if 5xx <1% and p95 <500ms we'll start rollback of cap.
liz-acc: customer confirms decreased errors but some background batch tasks still show timeouts. they asked for ETA.
oncall-sev: telling them we expect stabilisation within 30-60 minutes after reroute and cap.
mari-dev: added alert threshold for OrchidNova specifically: 5xx >3% will re-pager.
oliver-sre: logs show a small subset of requests still hitting pool-7 due to pinned sessions. scheduling a maintenance window to migrate pinned sessions at 11:30 PT if issues persist.
jia-eng: proactive step: start a script to drain connectors on nodes 7-9 gradually, migrating session state to pool-2:
```python
# pseudo
for n in nodes(7,8,9):
  set_drain(n)
  wait_until_inflight < 10
  migrate_sessions(n, target_pool='us-west3-pool-2')
```
oliver-sre: holding off drain for now since migration risks more cold starts. we'll coordinate with customer for the maintenance window.
liz-acc: customer agrees to the 11:30 PT migration window and will pause batch job beforehand. they requested a post-mortem.
oncall-sev: assign post-mortem to oliver + jia. include timeline, root cause, mitigation, and recommended platform changes (per-tenant backpressure, better KV quotas).
moliver: (typo)
oliver-sre: noted. creating incident ticket INC-2026 and assigning owners.
mari-dev: note for PMs: consider adding per-tenant soft GPU reservations and a runaway-job detector for dedicated pools.
jia-eng: also flag for Optimize team: suggest automated job humps detection and proactive routing suggestions.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 updated: status = stabilizing.
mari-dev: final check: last 10 minutes 5xx avg 0.9%, p95 380ms, eviction rate normalized. no new pagers.
oncall-sev: thanks team. leaving channel open until post-mortem draft ready.
liz-acc: I will send a customer summary email and include the mitigation steps and planned migration window. will follow up with PMs. :white_check_mark:
oliver-sre: prepping post-mortem notes now. will link when ready.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 resolved (stabilized) — please add any follow-up tasks to the ticket.
